text:
Sam: Heads-up — we've seen a new pattern in eu-west3 tonight: GPUs failing to attach for ~30s while the node's local NVMe iowait spikes. Appears correlated with the ephemeral janitor running full-pass on a subset of hosts.
Maya: I saw that too. 20% of batch attach failures map to the scrub window between 02:00-02:10.
Jen: Any logs? I want to see iostat / dmesg around the attach timestamps.
Sam: Pasted a compact excerpt: 
```
2026-03-19T02:03:11Z node-az3 nvme0n1: ios 2400/150/0, rq 32, iowait 87%
2026-03-19T02:03:12Z kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1
2026-03-19T02:03:14Z gpu-provisioner: attach timed out after 30s
```
Oliver: That's pretty bad. Are these hosts on the same scrub cadence? Could be a scheduling collision.
Maya: Yes — janitor target windows got aligned after a schedule change last week. We rolled the scrub uniformity change to reduce tail but it aligned windows in eu-west3.
Sam: Hypothesis: concurrent fstrim / deep-scrub + metadata compaction causing write bursts that starve small random IO, causing NVMe internal GC and thermal spiking => increased latency => attach failures.
Alex: Do we have telemetry for NVMe internal queues / SMART events around those times? Need to confirm firmware GC behavior.
Sam: We have SMART spikes and firmware counters bumping on ~12 hosts. I'll attach the aggregated counters to the incident later. For now, quick mitigation options:
  1) Stagger janitor windows by AZ (simple config tweak).
  2) Add an ephemeral io_smooth backoff to janitor: rate limit trim/write throughput when GPU attach rate > X.
  3) Canary a reduced-scrub mode (metadata-only) for a subset of hosts during the high-attach window.
Jen: Staggering sounds lowest-risk. How fast can we roll?
Maya: I can change the cron-tiling config in the janitor service to add a random jitter per host (0-10m) and target AZ distribution. Will test in staging first.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: janitor-config-change -> canary (staging) -> eu-west3 canary (10%)
Oliver: Also propose a runtime guard in the GPU provisioner: if node iowait > 60% for 10s, failfast with a retry after 20s instead of long attach wait. That prevents blocking user requests and surfaces transient backoff.
Alex: +1. Short circuiting will reduce tail latency and avoid holding scheduling locks. We should track attach-fail metric after adding this.
Sam: Action items: Maya to push jittered schedule to staging (ETA 1h), Jen to add iowait-based fast-fail in provisioner PR (ETA EOD), Sam to collect SMART/firmware counters and post in this thread, Oliver to prepare rollout plan for eu-west3 canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
Maya: Starting staging patch now. Posting test logs in 30m.
Jen: I'll open the PR and link it here: https://git.redwood/infraprov/PR-482
Sam: Thanks. If staging looks good we can start eu-west3 canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC with the stagger enabled.
Oliver: We should also consider a longer-term change: janitor should be aware of cluster load signals (gpu_attach_rate, avg_iowait) and avoid heavy passes during high attach windows. Filed feature request: https://tickets.redwood/INFRA-2198
Alex: Noted — will add acceptance criteria for telemetry and automated holdouts.
Maya: quick test from staging (iostat snippet):
```
staging-node-3 iostat -x 1 3
avg-cpu:  %iowait  6.8
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 1.00 20.00 5.00 512.00 1024.00 48.00 0.01 1.05 0.95 1.10 0.40 9.00
```
Maya: staging jitter eliminated the synchronized spike, no attach failures in 3 runs.
Jen: great. I'll land the fast-fail PR after review.
Sam: OK — moving this to monitoring checklist. We'll reconvene after eu-west3 10% canary results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
